summary: Alternate-runtime execution of an obfuscated payload on require()
details: On require(), index.js brotli-decompresses a hex-encoded blob and pipes the decoded script into a `bun -` subprocess, resolving the Bun binary from /usr/local/bin/bun, $HOME/.bun/bin/bun, and $BUN_INSTALL/bin/bun. The payload is shipped as opaque compressed bytes rather than readable source, and executes through a sibling runtime so the code path is not visible to Node-source review of the shipped file. The package advertises itself as a generic utility library, which does not require decoding and executing an embedded blob under an alternate runtime at module load. The current decoded content is a trivial console.log, but the delivery mechanism supports swapping in arbitrary code in any subsequent publish while keeping the Node-level file structurally unchanged. The package name has a placeholder/test shape (stream-buffer-utils-testmetest).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
